The week contains CPI, PPI, retail sales and the start of bank earnings, which are binary for rate-sensitive growth. High-beta semi and Korea pullbacks against strong prior relative trends look like position-driven overreactions rather than new fundamental breaks, but catalyst risk keeps conviction moderate.
portfolio_rationale: The strongest cross-sectional setup is the semiconductor complex (SMH, EWY, EWT) which gave back a large share of a strong prior relative trend in one week on unremarkable volume and without any supplied fundamental catalyst; I treat that as positioning-driven overreaction with modest positive expected excess return. Broader growth pullbacks (XLK, QQQ) are similar but smaller and stay below the 55% threshold given CPI/PPI rate risk. Recent winners (oil, Brazil, cyber, real estate) lack in-window support beyond price action.
key_risks: Hot September CPI/PPI on Oct 14-15 pushing yields higher and extending the high-beta tech/semi drawdown; The Korea and semiconductor selloff reflecting an unreported fundamental or geopolitical event that persists; Bank earnings disappointments from Oct 13 triggering broad risk-off that hits beta 2+ holdings hardest; Energy shock escalation (Brent >$106) worsening stagflation and favoring defensives over growth
